administration_requirements: Confirm the patient's age group is 16 years or older.
Check consciousness, respiratory rate, oxygen saturation and blood pressure.
Check relevant renal and hepatic history.
Check which medicines have already been administered.
Record medication name, dose, route, time, staff member and response.
High-risk medicines require senior RP clinician authorisation.

indications: Severe acute pain where opioid analgesia is appropriate

adult_dose.repeat: Only after reassessment and according to the authorised pathway or local RP protocol
adult_dose.dose_adjustment: Use a reduced dose in older, frail or opioid-sensitive patients

medications.rp_display_dose: 1-10 mg IV slowly over 4-5 minutes; maximum initial loading dose 15 mg. RP-ONLY DOSE.
do_not_give_if: Acute severe asthma or severe obstructive airway disease
Acute alcoholism or significant alcohol intoxication
Suspected raised intracranial pressure or serious head injury without senior authorisation
Severe uncontrolled hypotension or shock without senior authorisation
cautions: Previous opioid dependence or opioid tolerance

action: Escalate immediately to the senior RP clinician.
Consider naloxone according to the naloxone medication entry.

indications: Major trauma with suspected significant haemorrhage
Major trauma with a high risk of significant haemorrhage

adult_dose.time_limit: Give as soon as possible and normally within 3 hours of injury

medications.rp_display_dose: 1 g IV over 10 minutes, followed by 1 g IV infusion over 8 hours. RP-ONLY DOSE.
do_not_give_if: More than 3 hours since injury unless a senior clinician documents a specific reason
History of seizures unless specifically authorised
Severe renal impairment without an approved renal-adjusted protocol
cautions: Uncertainty about the time of injury
required_pre_administration_checks: Evidence of active or suspected major bleeding
medications.administration_warning: Do not administer rapidly as an undiluted IV bolus in the RP system. Record the start and completion time of the infusion.

concentration_examples: 400 micrograms/mL solution for injection or infusion
indications: Suspected opioid toxicity with respiratory depression
Suspected opioid overdose with inadequate airway protection

adult_dose.repeat: Repeat small doses every 60 seconds according to response
adult_dose.severe_toxicity: Larger cumulative doses may be required in severe toxicity or potent-opioid exposure
adult_dose.intramuscular: 400 micrograms IM when IV or IO access is unavailable
adult_dose.infusion: Requires senior clinician authorisation and an appropriate infusion protocol

medications.rp_display_dose: For opioid-related respiratory depression, give 100-400 micrograms IV/IO and titrate to adequate breathing. Repeat according to the overdose pathway. RP-ONLY DOSE.
medications.treatment_goal: Restore adequate respiratory effort and airway protection, not necessarily complete reversal of unconsciousness or analgesia.
do_not_give_if: Normal breathing with no respiratory compromise
Known hypersensitivity unless the patient is in a life-threatening opioid emergency
important_adverse_effects: Seizures in complex or mixed toxicity
important_interactions: Reverses the effects of opioid medicines
May precipitate acute withdrawal in opioid-dependent patients
observation_requirement: Continue close monitoring after the last naloxone dose.
The observation period must be longer for long-acting opioids or recurrent respiratory depression.
Escalate if repeated boluses are required.
